betterCitation: Percy Bysshe Shelley, ‘Ozymandias’, lines 12 to 14, Rosalind and Helen, A Modern Eclogue; with Other Poems (C. and J. Ollier, 1819), p. 98
reason:
REFUTED ON THE NOTE, NOT ON THE QUOTATION. The three lines and the 1819 citation survive the attack; the note that would ship beside them is false in the one detail it exists to assert, and a note whose whole content is a claim about letter case must not get the letter case wrong.

WHAT THE NOTE SAYS AND WHAT THE PRINTING SAYS. The note reads: 'The first printing, in The Examiner of 11 January 1818, reads colossal Wreck, so the citation has been moved to the book in which Shelley gathered the poem.' I fetched Wikisource's transcription of that Examiner printing (The Examiner (London)/Ozymandias, 11 January 1818) and its closing lines run: 'No thing beside remains. Round the decay / Of that Colossal Wreck, boundless and bare, / The lone and level sands stretch far away.' The first printing reads COLOSSAL WRECK, both words capitalised, not 'colossal Wreck'. It also reads 'No thing' as two words in line 12 and carries a comma after 'bare' that the 1819 text drops. The note therefore states, confidently and in its own voice, a reading of a named printing that that printing does not have, on the very point of capitalisation it was written to explain. Under the standard the editor gave, that is worse than saying nothing. The note must be corrected before the line ships, and the correction is easy: 'The 1819 collected volume prints colossal wreck in lower case. The first printing, in The Examiner of 11 January 1818, reads No thing beside remains and Colossal Wreck, with a comma after bare, so the citation names the book in which Shelley gathered the poem.' That is accurate, carries no dash, and says plainly which printing the card is quoting.

THE QUOTATION ITSELF SURVIVES, AND I CHECKED IT AGAINST THE RIGHT BOOK. Wikisource's proofread transcription of the 1819 volume prints the sonnet under the heading SONNET. OZYMANDIAS., and its last three lines return character for character as proposed: 'Nothing beside remains. Round the decay / Of that colossal wreck, boundless and bare / The lone and level sands stretch far away.' Lower case w on wreck, no comma after bare, full stop after away, 'Nothing' as one word. So the verifier's correction of the proposal from 1818 to 1819 was the right move and rescued the wording; it simply misreported the 1818 reading while doing it.

THE LOCATOR CAN BE MADE BETTER. I counted the sonnet: lines 12 to 14 are right, and they are the closing lines, so the fame test holds on the strongest possible ground. The volume title is right as printed on the 1819 title page, Rosalind and Helen, a Modern Eclogue; with Other Poems, London, printed for C. and J. Ollier, 1819. The one thing the citation lacks is the page, and the volume's own table of contents as transcribed from the scan gives Rosalind and Helen 3, Lines written on the Euganean Hills 69, Hymn to Intellectual Beauty 87, Sonnet 98. The sonnet is the only one in the book, so p. 98 is this poem, and adding it turns a work-and-line citation into an edition-and-page citation. The betterCitation above is 138 characters, inside the 140 limit, leads with the author's name, and carries no dash.

WHAT ELSE I TRIED AND COULD NOT MAKE STICK. (1) The speaker trap, which the brief carries generally. The sonnet is a traveller's report and the 1819 printing sets no quotation marks around it, so where the report ends is undecidable on the page and the traveller is unnamed in every printing. There is no named speaker to put in parentheses, and inventing 'the traveller' would be adding to the page rather than citing it. The verifier's handling is right. (2) Misattribution. Ozymandias is Shelley's beyond dispute, published over the pen name Glirastes in 1818 and gathered under his own name in 1819; Horace Smith's rival sonnet on the same subject is a different poem with different words and is not what is quoted here. (3) Anthology drift. The lower case wreck is not a modernisation: it is the 1819 book's own reading, and it is the 1818 magazine that capitalises. (4) Scope and publishability. 1819, poetry, no warning needed, nothing graphic. (5) Gates. shipped.js on the exact line with 'Percy Bysshe Shelley': shipped [], near [], percy bysshe shelley at 0 of 3 for the year, not banned, not on personsAtCap, and he stands nowhere else in the month's verdicts. Tag Poetry is the form of the work.

SO THE RULING IS NARROW. Ship the quotation, ship the 1819 source, add p. 98 if the editor wants the stronger locator, but do not ship the note as written.
